prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_F:
Labour’s 2019 manifesto promises real change: a fair, green, democratic economy that puts wealth and power in the hands of the many, not the few, while reversing a decade of Conservative failure on living standards, public services, climate, and Brexit.

- Mission and values: Rewrite the rules of the economy so it works for everyone; take on vested interests, polluters, and tax-dodgers; tackle poverty and inequality; guarantee universal, high‑quality public services funded fairly.

- Green Industrial Revolution: Deliver most emissions cuts by 2030; create 1 million good, unionised climate jobs; invest through a £400bn National Transformation Fund (including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund) plus a National Investment Bank and regional banks; delist climate‑wrecking firms; decentralise power and investment.

- Energy and ownership: 90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low‑carbon by 2030; ban fracking; mass home retrofit; expand wind, solar, tidal, storage, grids and heat networks; public ownership of energy, water, rail and mail to end rip‑offs and reinvest surpluses.

- Transport: Publicly owned, integrated rail with electrification and HS2 to Scotland; Crossrail for the North; better freight, cycling and walking; empower councils to own/regulate buses and restore routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils take control; accelerate EV transition and charging; aim to end new combustion car sales by 2030.

- Environment and food: Clean Air Act, flood defence boost, nature restoration, stronger protections; Right to Food, halve food bank use in a year and end need in three; net‑zero food by 2040; producer responsibility and recycling; end cruel wildlife practices.

- Fair funding and tax: Restore public services with a £150bn Social Transformation Fund; crack down on avoidance; reverse some corporation tax cuts; raise income tax only above £80,000; no VAT rise; insource services and end PFI.

- NHS and care: 4.3% average annual health funding rise; end privatisation; free prescriptions and basic dentistry; expand mental health and public health; build a National Care Service with free personal care and ethical provision.

- Education: National Education Service with free lifelong learning; restore Sure Start (Sure Start Plus), 30 hours free preschool for 2–4s; properly fund schools, end SATs, Arts Premium, enrich curriculum; bring academies/free schools under local democratic control; abolish tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.

- Work and rights: Real Living Wage of at least £10 for all; sectoral collective bargaining; day‑one rights; end zero‑hours; strengthen unions; move toward a 32‑hour week within a decade with no loss of pay; enforce via a new Workers’ Protection Agency; Inclusive Ownership Funds for workers; UBI pilots.

- Social security and equality: Replace DWP with a supportive Department for Social Security; scrap Universal Credit and punitive sanctions; lift disabled and carers’ support; uphold women’s, BAME, disabled and LGBT+ rights with stronger enforcement and a new Department for Women and Equalities.

- Housing: Build over 1 million social homes in a decade (100,000 council homes a year by end of Parliament); end Right to Buy; renters’ rights with rent controls, open‑ended tenancies and national licensing; leasehold abolition; end rough sleeping in five years.

- Policing and justice: Rebuild neighbourhood policing; tackle institutional bias; restore legal aid, probation in public hands, and invest in prevention; humane borders, end the hostile environment and indefinite detention; safe routes for refugees.

- Democracy: Abolish the House of Lords for an elected Senate via a Constitutional Convention; extend the vote to 16; automatic voter registration; curb dark money and lobbying.

- Brexit: Final‑say referendum within six months, with a credible leave deal that protects jobs, rights and peace, versus remain; implement the people’s decision.

- Internationalism and defence: Put peace, human rights and climate at the core; War Powers Act; suspend arms sales used to violate rights (e.g. in Yemen) and recognise Palestine; maintain NATO, renew Trident while pursuing multilateral disarmament; restore UK climate leadership and 0.7% aid focused on justice.

It’s time for real change—for the many, not the few.

TEXT_D:
Liberal Democrats 2019 Manifesto – Summary (ideological framing preserved)

Core values: Build and safeguard a fair, free and open society. Disperse power, protect liberty, equality and community, champion human dignity, creativity and diversity. Government’s role is to enable people to thrive and take part in decisions affecting their lives.

Stop Brexit, choose openness: The Lib Dems are the unapologetic party of Remain. A Lib Dem majority would revoke Article 50; otherwise they will back a People’s Vote with the option to stay. Remaining delivers a £50bn “Remain Bonus” to invest in schools and tackling inequality, protects jobs, the NHS, science, peace in Northern Ireland, UK unity and freedom of movement.

A stronger, fairer, innovation-led economy:
- £130bn for climate-friendly infrastructure: transport, energy, schools, hospitals and 300,000 homes a year (100,000 social).
- UK2050: lift R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapults; spread innovation beyond the South East; ethical tech via a Lovelace Code; citizen benefit from data; support creative industries.
- Skills Wallets: £10,000 for every adult for lifelong learning; expand high-quality apprenticeships; a Skills & Training Levy.
- Wellbeing Budget: judge policy by wellbeing as well as GDP.
- Fair taxes: restore Corporation Tax to 20%; replace Business Rates with a land value-based Commercial Landowner Levy; stronger action on multinational tax avoidance and tech giants.

Future of work and responsible business:
- New “dependent contractor” status with basic rights; flexible working from day one; higher minimum wage premium for zero-hours; union access; enforce prompt payment; employee voice on boards; duty of care on environment and human rights in supply chains.

Climate emergency and nature:
- Net zero by 2045; 80% of electricity from renewables by 2030; ban fracking; £12bn for clean power.
- Insulate homes by 2030; zero‑carbon new homes by 2021 (rising to Passivhaus by 2025); end fuel poverty by 2025.
- Clean transport: EV-only new cars/vans by 2030; rail network ultra‑low‑emission by 2035; fares freeze; more buses, trams, cycling; Clean Air Act.
- Nature Act with binding targets; 60m trees/year; peatland and wetland restoration; 50% UK waters protected; circular economy and zero‑waste laws (deposit returns, right to repair).

Education and childcare:
- Free, high‑quality childcare: 35 hours/week, 48 weeks/year from 9 months for working parents; triple Early Years Pupil Premium; £1bn for Children’s Centres.
- Reverse school cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; fix SEND funding; scrap SATs and league tables; replace Ofsted; protect arts; “curriculum for life.”
- FE uplift; restore maintenance grants; Student Mental Health Charter.

Health, mental health and care:
- 1p on Income Tax (raising £7bn/year) ringfenced for NHS and social care; £10bn capital; integrate services; end automatic tendering.
- Mental health parity: new waiting time standards, 24/7 crisis care, perinatal support; free prescriptions for chronic MH conditions; implement Mental Health Act reforms.
- Support carers with respite, higher earnings threshold; ethical international recruitment; more GPs and multidisciplinary teams.
- Public health first: Wellbeing Strategy; Clean Air right; obesity and alcohol harm reduction; regulate cannabis via a legal, licensed market; decriminalise abortion UK‑wide; PrEP access.

A fair society: dignity, security, homes
- Fix Universal Credit: first payment in 5 days; scrap two‑child limit and benefit cap; right to food; raise Local Housing Allowance; abolish bedroom tax; humane disability assessments.
- Housing: build 300,000 homes/year incl. 100,000 social; zero‑carbon standards; Rent‑to‑Own; 3‑year tenancies; tackle second homes; end rough sleeping in 5 years.
- Rural/coastal: buses, broadband, local hubs.

Safe communities, smart justice:
- Public health approach to violence; restore community policing; invest in youth services; Online Crime Agency; end disproportionate stop and search.
- Reduce reoffending: presumption against short sentences; more rehabilitation; women’s justice reform.

Rights, equality, and humane migration:
- Defend the Human Rights Act/ECHR; curb mass surveillance and police facial recognition; expand equality protections (GRA reform, X passports, BSL Act, end period and “pink” taxes).
- Scrap the hostile environment; 28‑day detention limit; right to work after 3 months; fair visas; welcome refugees (including 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years).

Better politics and devolved power:
- Proportional representation (STV), votes at 16, EU citizens’ votes, Lords reform; citizens’ assemblies; party‑funding transparency.
- A federal UK, stronger devolution and local fiscal powers.

A better world:
- Lead with allies through the EU, UN, NATO; keep 0.7% aid; Magnitsky‑style sanctions; suspend arms to Saudi; recognise Palestine; protect Hong Kong BNOs; cyber‑defence; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; global climate leadership.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_F" | "TEXT_D"
}
